metas.name: Argentina Wild Sunflowers
metas.note: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentine Tree Plantations
metas.note: Along the border with Uruguay in Entre Rios and Corrientes is where you'll most commonly find tree plantations in Argentina. There may be others rarely in other parts of these provinces/Argentina.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Bariloche
metas.note: Bariloche is a famous resort town in Nuequen. It can be recognized by the ski town vibes, the lake, and the mountains. While there are some other similar towns in Southern Argentina, Bariloche stands out and can be recognized with practice!
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Boat Coverage Entre Rios
metas.note: Just north of Buenos Aires City near Villa Paranacito there is boat coverage that is recognizable with the foliage and sometimes visible architecture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Buenos Aires Black and Yellow Taxi
metas.note: Black taxis with yellow rooftops can be seen commonly in the capital of Buenos Aires. While they should be unique to Buenos Aires Similar but distint taxis can be found in other cities.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Buenos Aires Small Ponds
metas.note: Small ponds near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Cardon Cacti
metas.note: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Chaco/Formosa - Sandy Soil and Vegetation
metas.note: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Comodoro Rivadavia
metas.note: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Cordoba Taxis
metas.note: Taxis in Cordoba are often all yellow or all green. May be seen uncommonly in other towns but if you're in a very large city with similar taxis it's likely Cordoba.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Eastern Santa Cruz Snow Coverage
metas.note: Snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Green Hills of Buenos Aires
metas.note: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Jujuy Province
metas.note: The northern province of Jujuy has unique architecture similar to that of the brick buildings in Bolivia and Peru.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: La Pampa T-Intersection Sign
metas.note: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these usually yellow (rarely other colors) rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, usually the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Latvian Style Hook Poles
metas.note: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza. (A bit more common in La Rioja, which also has a drier, more desert-like feel)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Misiones Red Soil
metas.note: The soil in misiones is a distinct red color (similar to the Brazil across the border). This combined with the vegetation in the area can be a good clue for this region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.note:
The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on state road 23.

NOTE: They are seen on the other side in Chile as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Pampas Grass
metas.note: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Pink Trumpet Tree
metas.note: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as Orán, Tartagal, General Mosconi and Salvador Mazza.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: RN40 Low-Quality Sunset
metas.note: Sunset coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with Neuquén.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: RN68 Red Mountains
metas.note: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: San Luis
metas.note: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: South-Central Saw Dust Car
metas.note: The “sawdust” car is found in centre-south Argentina (mostly west Rio Negro) and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Southern Argentina
metas.note: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: The caldén
metas.note: Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Toothpick Cactus
metas.note: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Tucuman Pole Stickers
metas.note: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in Tucumán.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Ushuaia
metas.note: The southernmost city of Argentina, Ushuaia, is easily recognizable by the snowy mountains to the north, the archictecture, and the vegetation.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Ushuaia Region - Tierra Del Fuego
metas.note: Well forested mountainous areas around Ushuaia in Southern Tierra Del Fuego are easily recognized.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Valdes Peninsula Wide Dirt Roads
metas.note: Unusually wide dirt roads and flat geography make the Valdes peninsula of Eastern Chubut recognizable.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Villa Dique Florentino
metas.note: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.
